newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Socialists call for talks on early poll.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Socialists call for talks on early poll.

text.p: Bulgaria's beleaguered ruling Socialists, saying the country was in "an explosive situation", called on opposition parties on Wednesday to meet to set a date for early elections.

Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev said on television that opposition parties must understand the depth of the crisis and that a new government he is trying to form should function for only three to five months.

"The chaos and power vacuum may cause a threat to civil peace," he warned in the interview on state television. "The deadlock is so complicated and the confidence in the government so low that the only alternative is new elections."
He called on politicians from all parties to "sit around the table and negotiate a date for elections".

The Socialists have run a caretaker cabinet since December 21 when prime minister Zhan Videnov resigned. Dobrev has been given a mandate to form a new cabinet but opposition parties and students have staged demonstrations for 24 days demanding immediate elections.
